Built-in middleware

Rate limiting

Fixed-window rate limiting keyed by client IP, with X-RateLimit headers, 429 responses and a pluggable store.

What rateLimit() does#

rateLimit() counts requests per client in a fixed time window and rejects callers who exceed the limit with a 429. It sets the standard X-RateLimit-* headers and a Retry-After header on the rejection.

js
import { createApp, rateLimit } from 'routiva';

const app = createApp();

app.use(rateLimit({ windowMs: 60_000, max: 100 }));

Options#

OptionDefaultMeaning
windowMs60000Window length in milliseconds
max100Maximum requests per window (alias: limit)
statusCode429Status code of the default rejection
message'Too Many Requests'Message in the default JSON rejection
headerstrueEmit X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After (set false to disable)
skip() => false(req, res) => boolean; return true to bypass counting
keyGeneratorclient IP(req, res) => string; the counter key
handlerundefined(req, res, next, record) => void for custom rejections
storenew MemoryStore(windowMs)Counter backend implementing hit(key)

The algorithm#

The default store uses a fixed window per key. Every request increments the counter; the window resets after windowMs.

text
hit(key)
  │
  ├─ no record, or record.resetTime <= now?
  │      record = { count: 0, resetTime: now + windowMs }
  │
  ├─ record.count += 1
  └─ return { count, resetTime }

limiter(req, res, next)
  │
  ├─ skip(req, res)? ─▶ next()
  ├─ record = store.hit(keyGenerator(req, res))
  ├─ remaining = max(0, max - record.count)
  ├─ over limit? record.count > max
  │      ├─ set Retry-After, call handler(...) or send statusCode JSON
  │      └─ stop
  └─ next()

The count is incremented before it is checked, so with max: 100 the 101st request in a window receives the 429. A fixed window is cheap but allows a burst at a boundary: a client can send max requests just before the reset and another max just after. For smooth limits, keep the interface and swap in a sliding-window store.

Response headers#

When headers is true (the default), every request through the limiter gets:

HeaderValue
X-RateLimit-Limitmax
X-RateLimit-Remainingmax(0, max - count)
X-RateLimit-ResetWindow reset time in Unix seconds (Math.ceil(resetTime / 1000))
Retry-AfterSeconds until reset, at least 1 — only on the 429 response

Set headers: false to suppress all of them, including Retry-After.

The default rejection is JSON, using statusCode and message:

json
{ "error": { "message": "Too Many Requests", "status": 429 } }

The MemoryStore#

MemoryStore is a Map-backed fixed-window store exported from the package.

js
import { rateLimit, MemoryStore } from 'routiva';

const store = new MemoryStore(60_000);
app.use(rateLimit({ store }));
MemberDescription
new MemoryStore(windowMs = 60000)Create the store; starts an unref()'d cleanup timer
hit(key)Increment and return { count, resetTime } (resets expired windows)
reset(key)Delete one key; with no argument, clear the whole store
clearExpired()Drop every record whose resetTime has passed
sizeNumber of live keys
stop()Stop the background cleanup timer

The cleanup timer is unref()'d, so it never keeps the process alive.

Custom stores#

The middleware only calls one method: store.hit(key), which must return { count, resetTime } synchronously. reset, clearExpired and size are conveniences on MemoryStore — the limiter does not use them.

js
class RedisStore {
  constructor(windowMs) {
    this.windowMs = windowMs;
  }

  // Must be synchronous: the middleware reads the record on the same tick.
  hit(key) {
    const count = redis.incr(key);           // node_redis in sync-ish wrapper
    if (count === 1) redis.pexpire(key, this.windowMs);
    const ttl = redis.pttl(key);
    return { count, resetTime: Date.now() + ttl };
  }
}

Most real backends are async, but hit must stay synchronous. Do the async lookup in an earlier middleware, stash a { count, resetTime } on the request, and read it back from key inside hit.

Per-route limits#

A limiter is ordinary middleware, so attach it to one route and clamp sensitive routes harder than the global default.

js
import { createApp, rateLimit } from 'routiva';

const app = createApp();

const loginLimiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 15 * 60_000,
  max: 10,
  message: 'Too many login attempts. Try again later.',
  keyGenerator: (req) => `${req.ip}:${req.body?.email ?? ''}`,
});

app.post('/login', loginLimiter, async (req, res) => {
  // ...
  res.json({ ok: true });
});

A custom handler takes over the response completely. record carries the current { count, resetTime }:

js
app.use(
  rateLimit({
    max: 20,
    handler(req, res, next, record) {
      res.status(429).json({
        error: 'rate_limited',
        retryAfter: Math.ceil((record.resetTime - Date.now()) / 1000),
      });
    },
  }),
);

To disable limiting during tests, pass skip:

js
app.use(rateLimit({ skip: () => process.env.NODE_ENV === 'test' }));

How keys are chosen#

The default keyGenerator returns req.ip, falling back to req.raw.socket.remoteAddress, then 'unknown'. req.ip respects the app's trust proxy setting: with it off, it is the socket's remoteAddress; with it on, it comes from X-Forwarded-For (a number selects that many hops from the right). Behind a proxy, enable trust proxy or every caller shares the proxy's IP and the limit.

The default store lives in memory, so it counts per process. Multiple instances behind a load balancer each keep their own counters unless you supply a shared store.
